author: JAMES BIGGAM Staff Writer
title: Roundup: Rivard hits 1,000-point mark for Hazen | | timesargus.com
text:
HARDWICK – Hazen girls basketball star Kelsie Rivard waited a full week knowing that she only needed eight points to become the seventh athlete in program history to join the 1,000-point club.
Competing in front of a packed crowd Wednesday against U-32, the junior forward could have easily gotten nervy and succumbed to the psychological pressure after missing some routine shots early in the game.
But it was patently clear to everyone at “The Den” that there was no way to deny Rivard of her latest milestone achievement. It was her destiny.
And after being limited to a pair of points in the first quarter, Rivard embraced the spotlight and surpassed the 1,000-point mark midway through a 12-point outburst in the second quarter. She finished with a game-high 21 points on a night she’ll never forget, helping the Wildcats extend their winning streak to 10 games with a 55-30 victory.
“We seat close to 1,400 in the gym and it was packed,” Hazen coach Randy Lumsden said. “You couldn’t even park inside the school parking lot and people were parking down the street. So it was just a great showing by the community and it shows how much everyone here cares about their youth and basketball. You can look around and you can tell that basketball in the community of Hardwick is our livelihood. And we live, eat, sleep, breathe basketball.”
Two seasons ago Rivard’s teammate Caitlyn Davison hit the 1,000-point mark, following in the footsteps of former Hazen standouts Penny Libercent, Jen des Grosseilliers, Sophie Smith, Alicia Shedd and Becca Whipple. When the Wildcats claimed their first state title since 1991 during their 2024 playoff run, it was undeniable that Rivard was no ordinary freshman.
“Kelsie is definitely confident in her abilities – and she should be,” coach Lumsden said. “She’s just a competitor and she wants to go out there and she wants to win. For the most part, I don’t even think that she thinks about her opponents. She just goes out there and she’s thinking, ‘I’m going to do everything I can do on this floor to make sure we win the game.’”
Rivard scored a combined 49 points at the Barre Aud her freshman year and closed out her sophomore season with 741 career points. A few weeks ago she broke the program’s single-game scoring record by exploding for 43 points against Randolph. And she’s been a huge reason why the Wildcats have gone a combined 52-4 during her varsity career.
“Kelsie knows what she wants to do with these different individual goals that she has set,” coach Lumsden said. “But she always puts the team first. And if we need her to do something, that’s what she’s going to do. She’s not just stat-chasing and trying to break every record she can.”
Hazen’s Mya Lumsden finished with 16 points Wednesday, while teammates Isabelle Gouin (seven points) and Autumn Dailey (six points) helped round out a balanced offensive performance. Paige Parker and Payten Pecor scored nine points apiece for U-32 and teammate Megan Pittsley chipped in with six points. The Raiders entered the game as winners of four games in a six-game stretch, including high-quality victories over Oxbow and Harwood.
“You look at U-32's schedule and you could see the teams that they’ve played and they’ve won some good games,” coach Lumsden said. “And in their last North Country game their best player got hurt in the first quarter, so that really wasn’t indicative of who they are as a team. So we knew that they were athletic and they were going to come in and it wasn’t going to be just a pushover game – that's for sure.”
Rivard didn’t waste any time while opening the scoring with a putback, while Rheia Schall quickly answered with a bucket for the Raiders. Dailey wedged between a pair of U-32 defenders and scored before a fast-break layup by Lumsden gave Hazen a 6-2 advantage. Rivard assisted Lumsden down low, Gouin knocked down a foul shot and then Dailey stretched the lead to 11-2. Long-distance shots by Pittsley and Arianna Conti ended the 9-0 run by Hazen, which led 12-7 at the end of the quarter after a Lumsden free throw.
Rivard went 3 of 4 from the charity stripe at the start of the second quarter, but U-32 continued its comeback charge behind a Pecor bucket. A steal-and-layup sequence by Rivard left the Wildcats star just one point shy of reaching her big moment. And before fans could blink, Hazen served up a quick defensive stop and Rivard raced up the court and scored again to push her career scoring total to 1,001 points.
Rivard’s older brother Tyler, a 1,000-point scorer himself, presented her with the game ball during a brief midcourt ceremony to commemorate the memorable moment with the rest of their family. Rivard’s mother, Sue (Miknak) Rivard, pushed her scoring total to 1,316 points for North Country in 1996 and currently serves as an assistant coach for Hazen.
“When Kelsie was in third grade and she started playing basketball and we started going to the gym on Sunday mornings, you could tell she was going to be a special player and she had all the talent,” coach Lumsden said. “And then knowing her mom’s past being the all-time leading scorer at North Country when they were playing in the Metro, that was pretty impressive to score over 1,300 points. And then Kelsie’s brother was a 1,000-point scorer and had 1,000 rebounds during Covid, so he missed half a season. So they definitely have some great family history on the athletic side of things.”
Julia des Groseilliers hit a turnaround jumper when play resumed, Rivard made a pair of baskets and Lumsden added a putback, a layup and a foul shot to extend the lead to 30-9 entering halftime. Parker and Dailey both scored off the glass early in the third quarter and then Lumsden assisted Rivard for a layup. Parker stayed hot by making four straight free throws, but baskets by Lumsden and Rivard made it clear that Hazen didn’t want to play any cat-and-mouse games.
Field goals by Pittsley and Parker gave the visitors a quick burst of momentum, while Rivard countered with a 3-pointer and a layup. Following a Parker foul shot, des Groseilliers made a basket and Rivard assisted Lumsden to keep Hazen in cruise control. A last-minute runner by Pecor resulted in a 46-22 Wildcats lead to close out the third quarter.
Pecor completed a three-point play from the foul line and promptly scored again to kick off the fourth quarter. Lumsden and Gouin countered with four points apiece before a Schall field goal and foul shots by Taylor Thompson and Pittsley capped the scoring.
“Tonight was not the outcome we were hoping for as a team,” U-32 coach Olivia Mekkelsen said. “We came out flat in the first half and then we had more energy and effort coming out in the second half. Hazen is a tough opponent and one that we are not as familiar with because they are new to the Capital League this year. We have games coming up that we can win and we will have to compete as a team in each one. Bringing energy and effort to this next part of our season is crucial.”
U-32 will host Randolph at 7 p.m. Friday. Hazen will host Peoples Academy the same day in a battle between D-III semifinalists from last year.
According to coach Lumsden, it’s been a special treat to savor two 1,000-point moments for his athletes over the last few years. However, with Hazen just past the midway mark of the season, he’s also happy to place extra concentration on some big challenges on the horizon.
“This was something we’ve been looking forward to,” coach Lumsden said. “But now that it’s happened, we’re definitely ready to move on and now we can really focus on the team and what the team needs to do. And all of Kelsie’s teammates did an amazing job of helping Kelsie achieve this goal: She doesn’t do it on her own. And she knows that and she’s very thankful to her teammates. And Kelsie does a lot besides scoring. Everybody talks about what a great scorer she is, but she averages 15 rebounds, seven steals and four assists a game for us."
GIRLS BASKETBALL
Oxbow 29, Lyndon 23
BRADFORD - Braylee Phelps (nine points) and Makenna Houston (seven points) gave the Olympians a key offensive boost during Wednesday defensive battle against the Vikings.
Madison Newland and Grace Griswold scored six points apiece for Lyndon, which trailed 7-6 after the first quarter. Even though Oxbow only tallied five second-quarter points, the Olympians held LI scoreless during that eight-minute stretch and led 12-6 at halftime before extending its lead to 22-14 at the end of the third quarter.
Oxbow will travel to play Lamoille at 7 p.m. Friday. Lyndon will travel to play Harwood at 12:30 p.m. Saturday.
“Lamoille is extremely tough,” Olympians coach Barry Emerson said. “That’s a long ride and it’s going to be a real test for us. But we’re hoping we’ll be up for the challenge.”
BOYS HOCKEY
U-32 8, Mount Mansfield 1
MONTPELIER – Junior Jackson Scribner recorded a hat trick Wednesday and added a late assist as the Raiders bounced back from their only loss of the season in commanding fashion.
Camden Leno assisted Scribner with 4:12 left in the first period and then Scribner doubled the lead on a feed from Liam Weller with 1:31 on the clock in the opening period. Mount Mansfield sliced the deficit to 2-1 when Aidan Soutiere recorded an unassisted goal with 4:56 left in the second period. Two minutes later Scribner scored again on assists by Ethan Nease and Connor Leno for a 4-1 advantage.
Ryley Wright scored twice in a span of 22 seconds in the opening minutes of the third period, thanks to two assists by Austin Graves and one by Sabin Kitchen. Chase Lafaille assisted Gage Heise with 9:01 remaining before Camden Leno scored on an unassisted effort midway through the period.
Ethan Nease and Scribner assisted Camden Leno for another goal with 4:57 on the clock as the 10-1 Raiders prevailed by five goals or more for the sixth time this season. Cougars goalie Carson Jensvold made 21 saves, while Raiders netminder Grayson Nease finished with 27 saves.
U-32 will travel to play Burr & Burton at 5 p.m. Saturday. Mount Mansfield will host Burr & Burton on Feb. 4 at 6 p.m.
Harwood 4, Burr & Burton 1
WATERBURY - Griffin Nelson tallied two goals and one assist to help the Highlanders lock up Wednesday’s victory over the Bulldogs.
Nelson gave the hosts a 1-0 lead on assists by Owen Farr and Eli Herrington with 11:59 left in the first period. Luke Lacroix made it a 2-0 game on assists from Farr and Cooper Browe with 12:49 remaining in the third period. The Highlanders added more breathing room midway through the final period when Herrington scored on assists from Nelson and Kaleb Vasseur. After a goal by BBA’s Miles Searles with 4:29 on the clock, Nelson closed out the scoring with 2:03 remaining on assists by Herrington and Lavit.
Harwood goalie Alex McCabe finished with 18 saves, while netminder Hunter Slade made 32 saves for BBA.
"The ice was tilted in our favor for most of the game, but we couldn't find the back of the net after that first early goal in the first period,” Harwood coach Matt Migonis said. “We were able to break the damn in the third, like we did Saturday night. And then we were able to pull away. I was very happy with our defensive game tonight, which is something we were hoping to improve on since the U-32 game. This was a good step in the right direction.”
Burr & Burton will host U-32 at 5 p.m. Saturday. Harwood will travel to play Spaulding the same day at 5:15 p.m.
Spaulding 6, BFA-St. Albans 4
ST. ALBANS – The Crimson Tide buried four third-period goals Wednesday against the Bobwhites to avenge an early-season 7-0 loss.
“It was a battle from the drop of the puck until the final buzzer,” Spaulding coach Brad Spaulding said. “The boys needed a little redemption after the last time we faced BFA.”
Drew Laprade (three goals, one assist) and Clayton Bell (one goal, three assists) led the way for the Granite City crew. Parker Harrington (one assist) and Elliott Caswell also scored in the winning effort and teammate Ethan Fortin made 33 saves between the pipes.
Brody Tatro and Duffy Smith both recorded one goal and one assist for BFA, while Bobwhites goalie Zach Merchand made 15 saves. Spaulding will host Harwood at 5:15 p.m. Saturday. BFA-St. Albans will travel to play CVU the same day at 5:15 p.m.
GIRLS HOCKEY
Chittenden 3, U-32 2
BURLINGTON – Hannah Drury tallied her 100th career goal for the Raiders, but it wasn’t enough as the Division-I Charge held off the D-II visitors.
Chloe Pembroke also scored for U-32 and teammate Emily Tringe notched two assists. Addi Fernandez and Taylor Davidson both notched one goal and two assists for the Charge and teammate Brett Mears scored her first goal at the high school level. A Fernandez goal gave Chittenden the lead for good midway through the third quarter.
U-32 goalie Addie Croteau made 40 saves, while Logan Jewett turned aside 26 shots for the hosts.
“We played hard tonight,” U-32 coach Josh Demers said. “I was very proud of the way we played and we just came up a bit short. But it was a great game to build on.”
U-32 will host Harwood at 2:30 p.m. Saturday. Chittenden will host the Kingdom Blades the same day at 2:20 p.m.
Burr & Burton 3, Spaulding 2
MANCHESTER – The Bulldogs were hot out of the gate Wednesday and extinguished a late surge by the visitors to snap the Crimson Tide’s eight-game winning streak.
Burr & Burton’s Mya Duncan scored on a Brooke Brownlee assist with 1:45 left in the first period and Katie Brownlee doubled the lead with 12:24 remaining in the second period.
Spaulding closed the gap to 2-1 when Allison French assisted Maddy Dukette with 11:49 left in the third period. Duncan scored a crucial insurance goal on an assist from Shelly Clark with 4:34 remaining and then Spaulding’s Katie Parker made it a one-goal game again on assists from Emily May and French with 2:16 left to play.
“We had some good scoring chances in the first two periods but could not convert,” Tide coach Brian Wilkin said. “We battled back in the third from two goals down twice to get within a goal, but we ran out of time.”
Spaulding goalie Gabrielle Bock finished with 28 saves, compared to 13 stops by BBA netminder Charlotte Salo. Spaulding will host Hartford at 3:15 p.m. Saturday. Burr & Burton will host Essex on Feb. 4 at 5 p.m.
“The line of Emily May, Maddie Dukette and Katie Parker had a good night,” Wilkin said.
Harwood 10, Brattleboro 0
WATERBURY – The Highlanders fired home five goals in the opening period and delivered a lights-out defensive effort during Wednesday’s shutout victory over the Bears.
“I was happy with our play tonight and it was great to score some goals,” Highlanders coach Eric Boyden said. “And I told our group that I was more proud of their defensive effort and keeping Brattleboro off the scoresheet.”
Briden Merrill and Jocelyn Bellanca both recorded three goals and two assists in the winning effort. Harwood also featured solid offensive contributions from Raine Diller (two goals), Alexandria Isham (one goal, two assists), Zoe Duffy (one goal, one assist), Emily Hill (two assists) and Jocelyn Brauer (one assist)
Highlanders goalie Camille Edgecomb made 18 saves, while netminder Dakota Vonfeldt stopped 41 shots for the Bears. Harwood will travel to play U-32 at 2:30 p.m. Saturday. Brattleboro will travel to play Stowe the same day at 4:15 p.m.
